page: Microsoft Azure D248ds_v7 is a massive general-purpose virtual machine within the Ddsv7 family, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. Designed for massive enterprise demands, it operates on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and supplies 248 dedicated vCPUs. Accompanying this processing footprint is 992.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not feature GPU accelerators.

A key characteristic of the D248ds_v7 is its integrated high-capacity storage subsystem. The configuration comes bundled with 15,120 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Premium Storage. This delivers low-latency scratch space and high input-output capabilities directly attached to the instance, eliminating network overhead for temporary operations. In addition, the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default.

From a cost-efficiency and operational perspective, deploying 248 dedicated vCPUs and over 15 TB of local fast storage concentrates an enormous amount of compute and storage density into a single host boundary. This reduces overhead across multi-node topologies, although the sheer size of the instance requires sustained high concurrency to avoid underutilization. With no GPU hardware, compute pipelines are constrained to standard CPU executions.

Microsoft Azure D248ds_v7 is best aligned with memory-heavy enterprise databases, large-scale data transformation, extensive batch processing, distributed caching tiers, and enterprise resource planning engines requiring massive single-node scale.
description: Microsoft Azure D248ds_v7 is a large-scale general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 instance family. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and an x86_64 Intel processor platform, it provides 248 dedicated vCPUs and 992.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. A central feature of this instance is its bundled 15,120 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, paired with Premium Storage support, which provides high throughput and low-latency disk I/O directly attached to the host. The instance excludes dedicated GPU acceleration and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Delivering vast resource density within a single node, the D248ds_v7 minimizes multi-instance coordination overhead for demanding applications. It is tailored for large enterprise databases, intensive ETL workflows, massive CI/CD pipelines, and high-concurrency enterprise applications.
